The complete Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with its Section 2 standing definitions and fixed scheme, on PDF page 2.

Use the periodic domain mathbbT = reals/(2*pi*integers) with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). For a periodic function f, hat f(k) = (2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx and <k> = (1+k^2)^(1/2). The Sobolev norm is ||f||_(H^s)^2 = sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s) |hat f(k)|^2. These spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms, with negative-order spaces interpreted as distributions. Reality means hat f(-k) = conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0) = 0. Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms use essential suprema.

Let S_t = exp(-t*partial_x^3), with Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3). Let P0 be the spatial mean and P = I-P0. Let D^(-1) = partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k != 0 and zero at k=0, and D^(-2) = (D^(-1))^2. The equation is
  u_t + u_xxx = (1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0.
The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation.

For timestep tau=T/L, the time-semidiscrete scheme is exactly
  u^0 = u0,
  u^(n+1) = S_tau u^n + F_tau(u^n) + H_tau(u^n),
where all products below are spatial products and [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0):
  F_tau(f) = (1/6)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)^2]
             - (1/6)*S_tau P[(D^(-1) f)^2],
  H_tau(f) = (1/3)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)*D^(-1) F_tau(f)]
             + (tau/9)*(S_tau D^(-1) f)*P0(f^2)
             - (1/54)*[S_(tau-s) D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1) f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
             - (1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s D^(-1) f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
This is the source scheme (2), with no spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0, there exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, this fixed scheme satisfies
  max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2) <= C*tau^gamma.
The constants are uniform over the entire stated initial-data ball and all permitted timesteps, with no Fourier-support restriction. The target includes all the hypotheses, quantifiers, endpoints, solution convention and method above.
spec.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact solution u and the fixed unfiltered scheme U defined below satisfy max_{0<=n<=L} ||u(n*tau)-U^n||_2 <= C*tau^gamma. The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. Both constants are uniform over the entire initial-data ball, all such L, and Fourier support.

definitions.definition: KdV is u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0, with real mean-zero data on Torus. An exact solution at regularity sigma>=0 means its unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^sigma) distributional solution obtained as the limit of smooth-data solutions. definitions.type: stepwise interpolation and residual construction from a smooth trajectory
definitions.definition: For tau>0, t_n=n*tau, and a finite smooth mean-zero trajectory f_n, on I_n=[t_n,t_(n+1)] put F_n(t)=F_(t_n)(t;f_n,f_n), z_n=f_n+F_n, C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f_n,F_n(s))ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(F_n(s),F_n(s))ds, W_n=Q_n(t_(n+1))+R2_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n), V(t)=f_n+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-((t-t_n)/tau)*W_n, and Y_n=V-z_n. For Interp, with constants C_M depending only on M,gamma,T, uniformly in n,tau and support: sup_(I_n)||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M, sup_(I_n)||F_n-F_(t_n)(t;v(t_n))||_(H^1)<=C_M*delta_n; sup_(I_n)(||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2)<=C_M*q_n; ||z_n||_(X(I_n))<=C_M; sup_(I_n)||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Dinv B_t(f_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_2<=C_M*q_n, ||Y_n||_(X(I_n))<=C_M*q_n and sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q_n. Here a_gamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2, 1/8 if gamma=1/2, and 0 if gamma>1/2. No numerical H^gamma norm is used.

Then, Interp satisfies sup_(I_n)||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty(I_n;H^(-pstar)))<=C_M*q_n. On any I=[a,b] contained in [0,T] with a a grid point, h=b-a<=1, define e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2. propositions.statement: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact solution u and the fixed unfiltered scheme U defined below satisfy max_{0<=n<=L} ||u(n*tau)-U^n||_2 <= C*tau^gamma. argument.text: Fix an arbitrary datum q and assume L1: q is real and mean-zero, belongs to H^gamma, and ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R. H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1, R>0. Reflection with a minus sign sends q to -q(-x) without changing any Fourier Sobolev norm. Apply E001's positive-regularity existence and uniqueness clauses at sigma=gamma, horizon T, and initial L^2 bound R; at smooth data apply them at every higher order as well, and uniqueness identifies these solutions. Its homogeneous bounds transfer to the inhomogeneous norms because 1<=<k>/|k|<=sqrt(2) for k!=0. Thus the source solutions have a common H^gamma bound depending only on T,gamma,R. E001's bound can equivalently be taken uniformly on the initial norm ball as stated in its bound clause.

argument.text: Set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). At (t,-x), u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx, so u_t+u_xxx=-U*U_x=u*u_x. Also hat u(k)=-hat U(-k), preserving reality, mean and all norms. The initial datum is q. Reflection is an involution, so source uniqueness transfers. The source coefficientwise integrated equation becomes distributional KdV under this change: products of L^2 functions are L^1, and each tested Fourier coefficient is absolutely integrable in time. Twisting by S_(-t) removes the linear term and gives v'=B_t(v,v)/2. Unitarity follows directly from the modulus-one multiplier; hence M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A(T,gamma,R).

produces.statement: u is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional KdV solution with datum q, v=S_(-t)u satisfies v'=B_t(v,v)/2, and sup||u||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R). For smooth q, u is smooth.

argument.text: For any two such initial data with L^2 norms summing to B0 or less, apply E001(iv) at theta=0 and horizon T to their reflected data. Twisting and reflection preserve the L^2 distance, giving sup||u-Utilde||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-qtilde||_2. In particular the real mean-zero Fourier truncations of q converge to q in H^gamma and L^2, stay in the same norm ball, and their flows converge uniformly in L^2; uniqueness identifies the limit with the flow just constructed. Thus this is exactly the prescribed smooth-approximation solution. The uniform H^gamma bound also passes to the limit by taking limits in every finite nonnegative Fourier norm sum and then their supremum. Discharge L1 and quantify q and the two-flow assertion; this proves every clause of N001.

argument.text: Fix tau,alpha,beta and assume L1: tau>0. If either phase is zero, eta=0 by the definition. Otherwise set h(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-M_tau(exp(-i*alpha*s)); then eta=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau h(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The estimate |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha|*|s-r| gives |h(s)|<=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau|alpha|*|s-r|dr<=tau*|alpha|. Therefore |eta|<=tau*|alpha|, and symmetry gives tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|).

produces.statement: For the fixed tau>0 and arbitrary real alpha,beta, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|), and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0.

argument.text: More sharply, |h(0)|<=tau*|alpha|/2 and |h(tau)|<=tau*|alpha|/2 by integrating r and tau-r. Also integral_0^tau |h'(s)|ds=tau*|alpha|. Integration by parts against exp(-i*beta*s) thus gives |eta|<=(|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau*|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta|. Interchanging alpha,beta proves the minimum of the two ratios. The zero-phase case already settled extends the result without dividing by zero. Discharge L1.

For the frequency assertion fix integers a,b,c,d and assume L2: abcd!=0 and a+b+c+d=0. The triangle inequality gives N1<=3*N2. Put A=|ab| and B0=|cd|. If d is among the largest two, min(A/B0,B0/A)/|d|<=1/N3. Otherwise the largest two are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, bound the minimum by B0/A and obtain |c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio is between 1/3 and 3; the remaining sizes |b|,|d| have maximum N3. Hence the expression is <=3*min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3. The b,c case is identical after exchanging a,b. Ties may be ordered arbitrarily and these alternatives still cover them.

produces.statement: Under L2, N1<=3*N2 and min(A/B0,B0/A)/|d|<=3/N3.

argument.text: For the second majorant, use the pairing (a,b),(c,d). If the largest two are in the same pair, the other pair has sum <=2*N3, while max(A,B0)>=N1*N2. Since a+b=-(c+d), |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=2*N3/(N1*N2)<=2/N3. If the largest two are in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, so max(A,B0)>=N2*N3; also |a+b|<=2*N1<=6*N2. The quotient is <=6/N3. Discharge L2 and universally quantify; together with the first two paragraphs this proves N003.

argument.text: Fix four sequences x1,x2,x3,x4 and assume L1: they are nonnegative and in ell^2(Z\{0}). First truncate to finite support. Partition the nonzero integers into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, and let Xshell_(r,j) be the corresponding ell^2 norm. Sum over the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices; relabel the sequence positions within one ordering so j1>=j2>=j3>=j4. The zero-sum relation implies the largest frequency <=3 times the second largest, hence j1-j2<=2. For each fixed pair of frequencies in the smaller shells, the sum over the remaining two with prescribed sum is at most the product of their ell^2 norms by Cauchy-Schwarz (a translated reflection preserves the norm). Each smaller shell has <=2^(j+1) integers. Taking their ell^1 norms by Cauchy-Schwarz gives a shell contribution <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr). Dividing by Nthird>=2^j3 leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr).

produces.statement: For each ordered interacting shell tuple, 0<=j1-j2<=2 and the weighted shell contribution is <=C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr).

argument.text: For q=j1-j2 in {0,1,2}, drop the upper restrictions on the smaller shell indices in this nonnegative sum. The resulting bound factors as C*(sum_J Xshell_(1,J)Xshell_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m>=0)2^(-(ell-m)/2)Xshell_(3,ell)Xshell_(4,m)). The first factor is <=||Xshell_1||_ell2||Xshell_2||_ell2. In the second, write r=ell-m and apply Cauchy-Schwarz for each r; it is <=sum_(r>=0)2^(-r/2)||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2=||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2/(1-2^(-1/2)). Shell orthogonality gives ||Xshell_r||_ell2=||x_r||_ell2. Summing the 24 orderings and three offsets proves the finite-support inequality with an absolute constant.

produces.statement: The asserted four-linear inequality holds with one absolute constant for all finite-support nonnegative inputs.

argument.text: For general inputs apply F002 to x_r restricted to |k|<=m and let m tend to infinity. Each norm is bounded by the full ell^2 norm. Every finite set of contributing quadruples is included at some m, and the nonnegative infinite sum is defined as the supremum of those finite sums. Therefore the same bound holds without exchanging conditionally convergent series. Restricting to any subset decreases a nonnegative sum. Discharge L1 and quantify the four inputs; this proves N004.

argument.text: Approximate each input by its Fourier truncations in H^sigma. Trilinearity and F002 bound every telescoping difference by a sum of one vanishing norm times two bounded norms. Thus the outputs are Cauchy in complete L^2, independent of the approximations, and define the claimed continuous extension and bound. At nonzero fixed output the coefficient is the same continuous limit of the polynomial formula. Discharge L1 and quantify these inputs.

Since ||f||_2<=M+1, the difference is <=C*tau*delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Adding the exact-data bound gives C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta). argument.text: For arbitrary mean-zero L^2 input f, Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2 and ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. More generally H^1 embeds into L^infty by the summability of <k>^(-2). For A,A2 in H^1, ||AA2||_2<=||A||_infinity||A2||_2 and partial_x(AA2)=A' A2+A A2', giving ||AA2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). These first hold for polynomials and extend by completeness. Since S_t is an isometry on H^s by its modulus-one multiplier, this proves ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. S_t also preserves reality and zero mode. Strong continuity follows by dominated convergence in the weighted square-summable Fourier series.

argument.text: For L^2 functions F,G, the convolution coefficient satisfies |hat(FG)(k)|<=||F||_2||G||_2. Thus ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2*sum_(k!=0)k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), which is finite since pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound and sum k^(-2)<infinity give ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1) gives ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. Finally, in J_t(A,g), bound S_t Dinv A in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infty using F001, proving the asymmetric estimate. These bounds justify the stated bounded extensions by polynomial density.

argument.text: Now fix arbitrary piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b] and a third such path h. On k!=0 the coefficient of J_t(f,g) is sum_(r+s=k)exp(-3*i*k*r*s*t)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiation of the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients, so d_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smoothness gives absolute Fourier convergence for every derivative used. Integrate and divide by three to obtain the normal form, summing over pieces if necessary; continuity makes the internal endpoints cancel. Symmetry is immediate. Because Dinv partial_x=P and S_t commutes with these Fourier multipliers, J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}. Integrating gives C_I(f,g,h) with no commutation through a product. At constant f,g the derivative terms vanish, giving Stage=[J]_a^t/6. Quantifying the inputs proves N006.

argument.text: For fixed tau>0, N006 gives Dinv:L^2->H^1 and the H^1 algebra bound. Thus Ftau is a continuous quadratic L^2->H^1 map. The first Htau term is a product of two inverse derivatives followed by P. The second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2), bounded by ||f||_2^2. The third has an H^1 cubic product followed by Dinv. The fourth has Dinv2 Ftau(f) and Dinv f, again an H^1 product followed by Dinv2; all coefficients, including tau^(-1), are finite for fixed tau. Hence Psi_tau is continuous from mean-zero L^2 to L^2. Every output is mean-zero: the first and third/fourth corrections have P or an inverse derivative; the mean of the second term is zero because Dinv f has zero mean. Conjugate Fourier symmetry and the real coefficients give reality. Smoothness is preserved by these operations, so finite smooth trajectories exist without any bound on their higher norms.

produces.statement: At each fixed positive tau the displayed Scheme is a continuous real mean-zero L^2 map and preserves smoothness.

argument.text: For any smooth input f at grid step n, identify source exp(t*partial_x^3) with S_(-t). The source Ftau,Htau formulas are exactly D008, term by term, with coefficients 1/6,1/3,tau/9,-1/54,-1/(27*tau), and identical endpoint signs. The source inverse derivative and mean have the same multipliers. In the twist, S_(-(t_n+tau))Ftau(S_(t_n)f)=F_(t_n)(t_n+tau;f,f), also following from N006's endpoint formula. The source cubic remainder has alpha=3ab(a+b), beta=3kc(a+b), the covariance eta and the prefactor -tau/(18ik), exactly R2. E005 therefore yields f_(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-R2^n_tau(f_n,f_n,f_n). Substitution in Interp makes Q_n(t_(n+1)) cancel with its part of W_n; hence V(t_n)=f_n and V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1).

produces.statement: For smooth Scheme trajectories the interpolation matches both step endpoints and the source remainder is exactly R2, with the sign in D021.

argument.text: Endpoint matching gives continuity across all grid points; all ingredients are spatially smooth and piecewise time-smooth. On a step F_n'=B_t(f_n,f_n)/2, C_n'=B_t(f_n,F_n), Q_n'=B_t(F_n,F_n)/2. Thus V'=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau. Since V=z_n+Y_n, expansion gives V'=B_t(V,V)/2-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. The last three terms are precisely rho_n' and hence mathcalR' on that step. The concatenation is continuous at its endpoints and starts at zero. The mean and reality properties follow from F001 and the real, mean-zero operators used throughout. Quantify the smooth trajectory and fixed tau to obtain N007.

argument.text: Write A=F_(t_n)(t;w,w), D=F_n-A. argument.text: The exact formula Dinv B_t(f,F_n)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F_n)] splits into the w product and the (f-w) product. argument.text: For the strong Y_n bound apply N006's normal form to C_n(t)=integral B_s(f,F_n(s))ds, using F_n(t_n)=0 and F_n'=B_s(f,f)/2. Symmetry of J and its cubic identity give exactly C_n(t)=J_t(f,F_n(t))/3-C_[t_n,t](f,f,f)/6. The first term is O_M(q) in L^2 by N006 and F001. argument.text: Because pstar>1, N006's mean-zero weak-norm comparison and F003 give sup||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q and sup||Y_n'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*q. argument.text: Assume L1: the step hypotheses of N008 hold, with q=tau^gamma+delta_n<=2. In rho_n's first integral apply N006's normal form to B(Y_n,z_n). Since z_n'=B_t(f_n,f_n)/2, the remaining integral is C(f_n,f_n,Y_n)/2 by N006. Apply N002's variable-path estimate with the negative slot on Y_n: its X norm is O_M(q), its negative norm is O_M(tau*q), and the constant f_n paths have bounded X and L^2 norms. Thus this integral is O_M(tau*q), for every partial step as well.

argument.text: For the second integral in rho_n apply the same normal form with Y_n in both slots. Its boundary is bounded by ||Dinv Y_n||_2||Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q^2; its derivative integral is bounded by tau*||Dinv Y_n'||_2||Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q^2. Since q<=2, these are O_M(tau*q). The endpoint correction is bounded by N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q. Thus sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q. N007 gives mathcalR'=-B(Y_n,z_n)-B(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. N006's negative-norm product bound and N008 give ||mathcalR'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*(q+q^2+q)<=C_M*q. Discharge L1, retaining the fully quantified step estimates.

produces.statement: Every qualifying step has sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*(tau^gamma+delta_n) and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty H^(-pstar))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+delta_n).

argument.text: Now fix I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, and assume L2: e=v-V has E_I<=1, with the smooth paths and M bound as stated in N009. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. From e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-mathcalR', ||e||_2<=E_I, ||v||_2<=M and the derivative part of F002 we obtain ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I). argument.text: Use N006's normal form, retaining both endpoints, together with e'=B(e,g)-mathcalR' and g'=B(v,v)/2-B(e,g)/2+mathcalR'/2. In the differentiated J terms, symmetry gives C(e,g,g)-C(e,g,e)/2=C(e,g,V), because g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is C(v,v,e)/2. The forcing terms combine as -J(mathcalR',g)+J(e,mathcalR')/2=-J(mathcalR',V). Therefore exactly Fint(t)=[J_s(e,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/3-C_[a,t](e,g,V)/3-C_[a,t](v,v,e)/6+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(mathcalR',V)ds. argument.text: For any three qualifying paths f1,f2,f3, put Lcut=P_(<=N/3), Hcut=I-Lcut. The trilinear telescoping expansion is C(f1,f2,f3)-C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Lcut f3)=C(Hcut f1,f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Hcut f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Hcut f3). The all-low product has no output above N. Projections contract both parts of X, while ||Hcut fj||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||fj||_2. In each expanded term apply N002 with the negative norm on its specified high input. Hence ||P_(>N)C_[a,t](f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product||fj||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product||fj||_(L^infty L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e). N009 yields ||e||_X<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I) and bounds the other X norms by C_M; the product of L^2 norms contains E_I. Their total is therefore <=C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

argument.text: For the forcing term, on each intersected step use the actual residual formula N007: integral J(mathcalR',V)=-C(Y_n,z_n,V)-C(Y_n,Y_n,V)/2-tau^(-1)integral J(W_n,V). The intervals here are the completed or partial intersection with the step. The first two are O_M(tau*q_n) by N002, putting its negative norm on Y_n, using N008's ||Y_n||_X<=C_M*q_n and ||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, and N009's bounded V norm on the intersection. argument.text: Combining F002-F004 gives sup||P_(>N)Fint||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. Use F001's low estimate and exact error identity, and N009's accumulated residual estimate, then take the time supremum.
